function: DRL update of hybrid analog and digital precoders for multi-user communication and moving-target sensing, trading spectral efficiency against CRLB (pp. 4, 7-8).
system: BS with ULAs of Nt=Nr=32, 3-bit phase shifters, 32 OFDM subcarriers at 28 GHz; up to 16 single-antenna users, one moving target (pp. 2-3, 11).
method: Actor-critic DRL (parameter-shared actor-critic with CNN state encoder), hybrid action space with user- or antenna-dimension incremental updates, offline replay-buffer training with adaptive critic-reliability loss (pp. 7-10).
data_channel: Authors' own SUMO intersection scene with Wireless InSite ray tracing and the doubly-selective model of Section II; joint GPS-CSI dataset, not released (pp. 3, 11).
test_conditions: Same generated dataset for training and testing; training curves at SNR 0 dB, U=8; evaluation sweeps over SNR, psi, number of users and velocity (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Opt-based SDR alternating optimization with perfect state, MP-based predictive precoding [20], Greedy [32], Random (non-learned); DRL w/o PSAC, called DQN in text (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Cumulative reward, averaged CRLB of the target angle, averaged spectral efficiency, SE-CRLB boundary, converging epochs, running time (pp. 11-14).
complexity: FLOPs-based orders in Table VII (actor forward pass linear in U; update O(Nt+M) or O(UM)) and running time per frame in Fig. 15 (pp. 13-14).
q1_support: p. 11: "communication and sensing channels for each symbol duration are generated using ray-tracing, based on the channel model outlined in Section II"; an own SUMO scene in Wireless InSite, not 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "We set SNR as 0 dB and U = 8" for training; p. 12: "schemes versus SNR after convergence" and sweeps over psi, U and velocity; the paper never states that a trained model is tested in an unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 12: "in the SE observed in non-PSAC architectures" (called DQN in the experiments) and "Compared to the training of the classic actor-critic" give the learned baseline; p. 11: "Predictive precoding scheme in [20]", the Opt-based and Greedy schemes are non-learned; compared on SE and CRLB (Figs. 7, 9, 12).
q4_support: p. 13: "We further compared the averaged running times within one frame of different schemes in Fig. 15"; Table VII (p. 14) gives FLOPs-based complexity orders for the proposed and benchmark schemes.
q5_support: p. 11: "We first construct a joint GPS-CSI dataset to simulate doubly dynamic vehicular network scenarios"; built by the authors with SUMO and Wireless InSite, and no code or data link is given.
notes: Included as area 5 (ISAC precoding). q1 is 0 because the channels come from the authors' own SUMO scene run in the commercial ray tracer Wireless InSite plus their Section II model, not from DeepMIMO, 3GPP or measurements; reviewer may check. q3 is 1 only through the baseline called 'DRL w/o PSAC' in Figs. 6, 9, 12 that the text calls DQN (p. 12); if the reviewer reads it as an ablation of the proposed method, q3 is 0.
